canonical_statement: For integers n and real p with 1 < p < n, put q = n*p/(n-p). Every compactly supported smooth real-valued function u on Euclidean R^n satisfies its L^q norm bounded by the optimal Talenti constant times the L^p norm of its gradient.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat, p q : Real, u : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real; exact Lean function-space encoding remains open
hypotheses: u is smooth and compactly supported
conclusion: norm_Lq u <= C_Talenti(n,p) * norm_Lp (gradient u), with C_Talenti(n,p) the least valid constant
degenerate_cases: n = 0 or n = 1 excluded by 1 < p < n
p >= n and the critical/endpoint embeddings excluded
u = 0 is allowed and gives the trivial boundary case
